newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive says may list Munter unit.
newsitem.headline: Incentive says may list Munter unit.

text.p: Swedish medical technology and investment company Incentive AB said on Monday it was looking into a listing of its Munter unit, which would be in line with its strategy to focus on medical technology.
It also said the six-month operating profit for its key medical technology unit amounted to 776 million crowns, up from 709 million in the corresponding year-ealier period.
Incentive posted a profit after financial items of 11.74 billion crowns, including a capital gain of 11.10 billion, which was in line with market expectations of a profit of 11.70 billion crowns.
In the first half of 1996, the group's profit after financial items amounted to 1.99 billion crowns.

Incentive divested three relatively large shareholdings in the first six months of the year, including 110 million shares of electrical engineering group ABB AB, or about half its stake, for a capital gain of 12.4 billion crowns.
"The sale of these shareholdings has contributed to the streamlining of the group and has strengthened its financial position," Incentive said in a statement.
Incentive said it would continue to focus the operations of the group on its core business of medical technology through the further sale of various business.

"The strategic transformation of the group during the period were substantial, resulting in a more streamlined and focussed structure, an improved financial position and a much stronger position in the core area of medical technology," it said.
In keeping with this strategy, Incentive said it was investigating a listing of its Munter unit, which it said is a leading manufacturer of dehumidifiers and humidifiers for industrial uses.
It said Munters, which is an independent company within Incentive had grown considerably and has a leading global position. Total annual sales are about two billion crowns.
It said thanks to hedging the effects of currency flows were negligible. Sales in the period fell to 10.31 billion crowns from 10.64 billion crown.
The share rose to trade up 12 crowns to 712 after the result was released compared to a rise of five crowns beforehand.
Operating profit for its medical technology unit rose to 776 million crowns from 709 million. Sales gained 18 percent to 6.34 billion crowns.
Adjusted for the acquisition of Vivra, a U.S. dialysis clinic with around 270 clinics and 16,000 patients, the increase in sales for the medical technology unit was 12 percent.
